question: Should OpenClaw accept static SecretRef values in `sandbox.docker.env` when the resolved values still become Docker environment variables visible through Docker/container metadata?
rationale: The source gap and implementation path are clear, but the permanent credential-to-sandbox exposure boundary is a maintainer/security decision rather than a pure code repair.

options.title: Accept with explicit boundary
options.body: Land the linked PR after confirming the Docker metadata exposure warning, SecretRef target registry, audit/configure behavior, and tests are aligned.

options.title: Require stronger warning first
options.body: Ask the linked PR to make SecretRef-backed Docker env metadata exposure more explicit in docs and review notes before merge.

options.title: Reject env delivery
options.body: Pause the linked PR and design a non-env secret delivery path if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable for SecretRef-backed values.

recommendation.title: Accept with explicit boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR after confirming the Docker metadata exposure warning, SecretRef target registry, audit/configure behavior, and tests are aligned.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh authored the closest merged Docker env propagation fix and is the strongest routing candidate for the exact env-to-Docker boundary.
